name: Mietwagen and taxi owner-operator compliance file (order book, return duty, TSE, per-trip records)
buyer: Small Mietwagen and taxi firms (owner-operators, 1-5 cars)
trigger: Federal tax rules (section 146a AO, KassenSichV): TSE required for taximeters and Wegstreckenzähler from 2026-01-01; MV tax portal says older certified devices must be retrofitted by 2027-01-01. Federal PBefG section 49(4): Mietwagen return duty with a booked record of order intake kept 1 year. Land/city licensing authorities check it (Berlin LABO checks TSE proof at licensing; proof due by 2026-09-30).
evidence: https://selbststaendigkeit.de/news-gruendertipps/tse-pflicht-taxis-mietwagenunternehmen/ ; https://www.berlin.de/labo/mobilitaet/fahrerlaubnisse-personen-und-gueterbefoerderung/aktuelles/artikel.1623029.php ; https://www.bielefeld.de/sites/default/files/dokumente/Mietwagenverkehr_Hinweis.pdf ; https://www.steuerportal-mv.de/static/Regierungsportal/Ministerium%20f%C3%BCr%20Finanzen%20und%20Digitalisierung/Steuerportal/Inhalte/Merkblatt%20f%C3%BCr%20Mietwagenunternehmen.pdf ; https://www.etl.de/aktuelles/taxi-und-mietwagenunternehmen-finanzamt-2026/ ; VGH München 11 ZB 20.2076 (warning upheld for missing order book entries)
existing: Competitor search (Software Mietwagen Auftragsaufzeichnung Rückkehrpflicht Fiskaltaxameter TSE Anbieter) found FMS with fiskaly cloud TSE (signs all dispatch data, per a 2024 Taxi Times article), Hale hardware TSE, Taxi.de booking software (passes orders to billing) and TAXI-Experte. None was described as covering the Rückkehrpflicht proof or a Finanzamt export. Vendors sell taximeter hardware, so the field is crowded around the TSE part.
unchecked: Number of Mietwagen firms; whether ride-hailing platforms (Uber, Bolt) and fleet back-offices already give drivers the order record; exact TSE dates per device type and Land; whether the Mietwagen Rückkehrpflicht is still enforced in the same way; vendor feature lists (read the vendor sites, not just 2024 article).

first_check.duty: The duty is real, federal and in force. Under § 49 Abs. 4 PBefG, a Mietwagen may only carry out orders that arrive at the firm's base. The firm must record each incoming order in a book or electronically and keep the record for 1 year. After each trip the car must return to the base straight away unless it already has a follow-on order. The current text on gesetze-im-internet.de still contains the return duty. On 2026-06-03 the BGH (I ZR 123/25) upheld the return duty as constitutional and held that breaching it is unfair competition. Enforcement is active. In VG Ansbach AN 10 S 26.536 (16.07.2026), the authority demanded the order register on USB plus machine-readable platform trip data with return times and follow-on order IDs. It counted 67 breaches in 210 trips and revoked permits for 16 cars without a prior warning, and the court upheld this. VGH München 11 ZB 20.2076 upheld a sanction for a badly kept order book. Separately, under § 146a AO, KassenSichV and the BMF letter of 11.03.2024, taximeters and Wegstreckenzähler need a TSE from 2026-01-01. Breaches can be fined up to EUR 25,000 (Härting). The device must also be reported to the Finanzamt via ELSTER within 1 month. One summary says older Wegstreckenzähler with a digital interface may be connected to a TSE until 31.12.2026. Härting and the Berlin LABO page give 1.1.2026 as the hard date. I could not resolve this because the MV Merkblatt PDF was unreadable.
first_check.market: I found no current national count. The DTMV figure via Statista is just over 53,000 taxis in Germany in 2016. The federal survey every four years (last cited for 31.12.2016) and Brandenburg's answer (data held only by districts) give no Mietwagen firm count. Mietwagen permits have no cap, and the Uber/Bolt-driven fleet segment is large in big cities. I estimate roughly 20,000 to 30,000 taxi and Mietwagen firms in total, mostly with 1 to 5 vehicles. This is unverified.
first_check.competitor: The TSE part is crowded: taximeter and Wegstreckenzähler hardware vendors, fiskaly cloud TSE through FMS (per the claim), and Hale. It should be left out of scope. For the order book, the FREENOW AGB require Mietwagen firms to record and forward orders through FREENOW's Fleet Partner Dashboard, so platforms already partly capture order intake. Uber's supplier portal manages the fleet, drivers and revenue. I found no evidence that it produces a § 49 order book. FahrerApp (meinfahrer.app) is Mietwagen-specific telematics with shift recording and seat-occupancy sensors. Its listing does not mention the order book, return-duty proof or TSE. SuE-TaMi Dispo, SOLU Driver and Taxi.de are dispatch tools. Fleetster, Vimcar and R-DRIVE are general electronic logbooks. I found no product that merges platform orders, GPS returns and follow-on order IDs into a register the licensing authority can audit and that flags return-duty breaches. The VG Ansbach case shows authorities now ask for exactly that data.
first_check.reason: The pain is real and rising. The BGH upheld the return duty in June 2026, and VG Ansbach shows permits revoked for a missing or incomplete machine-readable order register. Owner-operators face daily record-keeping. The weak points: the TSE part is solved by hardware vendors. Platforms (FREENOW dashboard, Uber portal) already hold most order data, so a tool would be an aggregation and audit layer. Some heavy Mietwagen users break the return duty on purpose and won't buy proof tools. Political proposals to abolish the return duty add regulatory risk. Buyers are fragmented, price-sensitive and reached through taxi associations or IHK. An MVP needs platform data imports and GPS, so it is not trivial. It is a niche gap worth testing but carries risk.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Partial overlap: Uber's supplier portal and FREENOW's Fleet Partner Dashboard record platform orders, and taximeter and Wegstreckenzähler vendors cover the TSE part. Not checked: whether platform exports satisfy authorities.
challenge_check.reason: Nothing I found kills the claim. § 49(4) PBefG has allowed electronic and app-based order logs since 2021, and the July 2026 amendment did not change § 49. The BGH upheld the return duty on 3 June 2026 (I ZR 123/25). VGH München 11 CS 26.1088 (7 August 2026) upheld revocation of 8 permits after the authority demanded the order book plus app order data on USB and ran a time-series analysis that found 50 return-duty breaches in 175 trips. I found no vendor selling an order book that checks the return duty. Uber's supplier portal and FREENOW's dashboard capture orders but do not check return compliance. The score stays low because many Uber and Bolt fleet owners avoid the duty on purpose, enforcement depends on the authority and is mostly triggered by suspicion, and reform lobbying continues. The TSE part is already crowded.
